catalog_quote: 1.3.4 Predictability of syllable division, stress, and position of vowel length within a phonological word. ... (ii) Stress : Heavy (tonic) stress is marked [ˈ] at the beginning of the syllable. Weak stress is left unmarked. A. Monosyllabic words have heavy stress. They are therefore unmarked. ... B. In disyllables, when the second syllable is closed and at the same time the first syllable has a vowel other than a, the second syllable is stressed. Examples. əˈsaḍ '(a lunar month)' tiˈhar 'festival' koˈṭhar 'store room' kuˈmhar 'potter' kʰəˈpər 'roof' ... əṅˈkal 'famine' ḍeṅˈgur 'ant hill' But ˈa.den '(a kind of tree)' ˈsa.vən '(a lunar month)' ˈna.ər 'plough' ˈman.tər 'however, but' In all the other cases the first syllable is stressed. Examples. ˈleṅ.ḍa 'tail' ˈbah.na 'husking pit' ˈgir.li '(she) fell' ˈkən.ki 'small pieces of uncooked rice' ˈa.kʰi 'eyes' ˈtu.i 'you(sg.)' ... C. Words …
